obligations.deadline: On the I-94 admit-until date. Escalate at 90/30/0 days remaining.
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(13)(i)(A) (validity + 10-day pre/post); 8 CFR 214.1(l)(1) (10-day grace); admit-until controlling per 8 CFR 214.1(a)(3); unlawful-presence bars INA 212(a)(9)(B) / 8 USC 1182(a)(9)(B).
obligations.data_needed: i94.admitUntilDate, i94.mostRecentEntryDate, petition.validityStart/End, visaStamp.expiry (informational), any pending extension receipt + filing date.
evidence_required: any pending extension receipt + filing date

obligations.check: Continuous maintenance of status: work only within the authorized petition window, keep a valid unexpired I-94, no unauthorized employment; an extension cannot be approved if status lapsed.
obligations.requirement: Every nonimmigrant must maintain status. An extension/amendment may NOT be approved for a beneficiary who failed to maintain status or whose status expired before filing (absent the discretionary late-filing excuse). May not work except during the validity period (plus §214(n)/240-day windows).
obligations.threshold: Maintained iff: (a) all employment within an authorized window (approved validity, OR 240-day coverage, OR §214(n) portability, OR a documented grace period); (b) I-94 not expired without a timely extension; (c) no unauthorized employment. A lapse breaks the chain and blocks future extensions/AOS.
obligations.deadline: Continuous (no single date).
obligations.data_needed: timeline of: petition validity windows, I-94 admit-until, all employment start/stop + employer/worksite, extension/port filing dates + decisions, grace-period invocations — the union of inputs from the other h1b.* rules.
evidence_required: grace-period invocations — the union of inputs from the other h1b.* rules

obligations.check: Days spent physically outside the U.S. (>24h) during H-1B validity can be recaptured and added back to the 6-year max — petitioner must request and document them.
obligations.requirement: Time >24h physically outside the U.S. during the validity of an approved H-1B petition is not counted toward §214(g)(4), regardless of whether the absence interrupted the stay. Remaining time may be recaptured in a later petition at any time before the full period is used. Petitioner's burden to request and demonstrate with evidence (passport stamps, I-94, tickets, a chart of dates abroad).
obligations.threshold: Recapturable = full days (>24h absences) physically outside the U.S. during validity periods. No temporal limit on claiming. Recapture of a cap-counted beneficiary does NOT re-subject them to the cap.
obligations.deadline: n/a (a credit). Claimed in/with the extension that needs the time.
obligations.data_needed: I-94 arrival/departure travel history (every entry/exit), per-trip duration, petition validity windows, evidence-inventory flags (passport stamps/tickets).

obligations.check: Total H-1B (+L) time ≤6 years; beyond 6 requires either a 1-year-abroad reset or an AC21 7th-year exemption.
obligations.requirement: An H-1B alien who has spent six years under (H) and/or (L) may not extend, change status, or be readmitted under (H)/(L) unless physically present outside the U.S. (except brief business/pleasure trips) for the immediate prior year. The 6-year cap is the statutory "period of authorized admission" under INA §214(g)(4).
obligations.threshold: 6 years (2,190 days) aggregate H-1B + L physical presence. Time >24h physically outside the U.S. during validity is NOT counted and is recapturable. Reset to a fresh 6 years requires 1 continuous year abroad.
obligations.deadline: On reaching the 6-year mark (net of recapture).
obligations.data_needed: all prior H-1B and L petition validity periods + entry/exit history (I-94 travel), daysPhysicallyOutsideUS per validity, anyContinuousYearAbroad (dates), proposedExtension.endDate.

obligations.check: H-1B petition (I-797) initial validity ≤3 years and ≤ the LCA validity period.
obligations.requirement: An approved H-1B specialty-occupation petition is valid up to 3 years but not beyond the LCA validity (DOD R&D/coproduction up to 5; fashion modeling up to 3). The I-797 dates are the outer bound of authorized employment.
obligations.threshold: ≤3 years (specialty); validity end ≤ LCA end. 5 years for DOD R&D/coproduction.
obligations.deadline: n/a (validity-ceiling check). Petition validity END date anchors downstream expiry/extension rules.
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(9)(iii)(A)(1); validity tied to LCA per 20 CFR 655.730.
obligations.data_needed: petition.receiptNumber, validityStart, validityEnd, classification (specialty/DOD/fashion), lca.validityStart, lca.validityEnd.

obligations.check: H-1B petition (I-797) initial validity ≤3 years and ≤ the LCA validity period.
obligations.requirement: An approved H-1B specialty-occupation petition is valid up to 3 years but not beyond the LCA validity (DOD R&D/coproduction up to 5; fashion modeling up to 3). The I-797 dates are the outer bound of authorized employment.
obligations.threshold: ≤3 years (specialty); validity end ≤ LCA end. 5 years for DOD R&D/coproduction.
obligations.deadline: n/a (validity-ceiling check). Petition validity END date anchors downstream expiry/extension rules.
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(9)(iii)(A)(1); validity tied to LCA per 20 CFR 655.730.
obligations.data_needed: petition.receiptNumber, validityStart, validityEnd, classification (specialty/DOD/fashion), lca.validityStart, lca.validityEnd.

obligations.check: An eligible H-1B beneficiary may begin new/concurrent employment upon the FILING of a nonfrivolous H-1B petition by the new employer — before approval — under AC21 §105 / INA §214(n).
obligations.requirement: Authorized to start concurrent/new employment under §214(n) upon the filing of a nonfrivolous H-1B petition, or the requested start date, whichever later. Eligible = (i) lawfully admitted/provided H-1B status; (ii) a nonfrivolous new-employment petition (with amend/extend-stay request) filed BEFORE the authorized stay expired; (iii) no unauthorized employment from last admission through filing. Authorization continues until adjudication; if denied, it ceases.
obligations.threshold: Work may begin on max(petitionFiledDate, requestedStartDate). Petition MUST be filed before I-94 admit-until expiry (an expired I-94 from a prior portability petition still counts as "period of stay authorized" for a successive port — bridge porting). Requires NO unauthorized employment since last admission.
obligations.deadline: n/a (enabling rule). Authorization runs until adjudication; denial ceases work authorization immediately.
obligations.data_needed: newPetition.filedDate, requestedStartDate, nonfrivolous (bool/attested), beneficiary.currentStatus, i94.admitUntilDate, beneficiary.unauthorizedEmploymentSinceAdmission (bool), priorPortabilityChain[].

obligations.check: To end H-1B wage liability and effect a "bona fide termination": (1) notify the beneficiary, (2) notify USCIS to withdraw the petition, and (3) offer return-transportation costs for an involuntary termination.
obligations.requirement: The required (LCA) wage obligation continues until a BONA FIDE termination. DOL/case law (Amtel) requires: (1) express notice to the employee; (2) notice to USCIS so the petition is canceled/withdrawn (withdrawal → immediate automatic revocation); (3) for an involuntary dismissal before the end of authorized admission, liability for the reasonable costs of return transportation to the last foreign residence. Until USCIS is notified, back-pay/wage liability can accrue.
obligations.threshold: All THREE prongs for a complete bona fide termination. Wage liability runs until at least the USCIS-notification prong. Return-transportation applies only to involuntary dismissals (not voluntary resignations). Separate 60-day grace (or until I-94 end) under 8 CFR 214.1(l)(2).
obligations.deadline: Promptly upon termination. Wage liability accrues until USCIS notification. Escalate at 1 / 0 days.
obligations.data_needed: employment.terminatedDate, termination.type (voluntary/involuntary), employeeNotice.given (bool)+date, uscisWithdrawal.sentDate, returnTransport.offered (bool)+date (involuntary), lca.requiredWage, wagesPaidThrough, beneficiary.lastForeignResidence.

obligations.check: On termination, withdraw the I-129 with USCIS and withdraw/cancel the LCA with DOL to stop ongoing obligations.
obligations.requirement: Approval is immediately and automatically revoked on a written withdrawal (or going out of business, or DOL LCA revocation). A petitioner no longer employing the beneficiary shall send a letter explaining the change to the approving director. Separately withdraw the LCA from DOL — though LCA withdrawal alone does NOT end wage liability; only a bona fide termination does.
obligations.threshold: Written withdrawal letter to the approving USCIS service center (→ immediate automatic revocation). LCA withdrawal request to DOL. No fixed day-count; promptly.
obligations.deadline: Promptly upon (bona fide) termination. The USCIS-withdrawal date caps continued wage-liability accrual.
obligations.data_needed: petition.receiptNumber, approvingServiceCenter, uscisWithdrawal.sentDate, lca.caseNumber, lcaWithdrawal.sentDate, employment.terminatedDate.

obligations.check: H-1B petition filed on/after 2026-04-01 uses Form I-129 edition 02/27/26 (not 01/17/25).
obligations.requirement: USCIS requires the 02/27/26 edition for all H-1B/H-1B1 petitions filed on/after April 1, 2026; prior-edition petitions received on/after that date are rejected. Before 04/01/2026 the 01/17/25 edition remains acceptable.
obligations.threshold: Edition date (lower-right corner) must read 02/27/26 for filings on/after 2026-04-01; cutover = 2026-04-01.
obligations.deadline: Hard cutover 2026-04-01.
obligations.citation: USCIS Form I-129 edition 02/27/26; form-edition acceptance policy on the I-129 forms page; PRA docket USCIS-2025-0040.
obligations.data_needed: petition.formEditionDate; petition.filingDate (or intended postmark); petition.classification (H-1B/H-1B1).

obligations.check: All five new position-requirement fields (Q7–Q11) on the H-1B Data Collection / H Classification Supplement are completed (non-blank).
obligations.requirement: On the 02/27/26 edition, answer Q7 education required; Q8 field(s) of study; Q9 years of experience required; Q10 special skills required; Q11 number supervised + their titles. Petitioners must answer every applicable Data Collection Supplement question.
obligations.threshold: 5 required fields, all non-empty (Q11 may be "0"/"None" but must be explicitly answered).
obligations.deadline: At filing (Section 2(a) of the Data Collection Supplement).
obligations.citation: Form I-129 (02/27/26), H-1B and H-1B1 Data Collection and Filing Fee Exemption Supplement, Questions 7–11 (form page 21); Instructions for Form I-129, H Classification / Data Collection Supplement section.
obligations.data_needed: hSupp.q7_educationLevelRequired; q8_fieldsOfStudy; q9_yearsExperienceRequired; q10_specialSkills; q11_numberSupervised + supervisedTitles.

obligations.check: Field(s) of study required (I-129 Q8) directly related to the duties and to a specific specialty (not a general degree).
obligations.requirement: Under 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(ii) (as amended eff. 01/17/2025), a specialty occupation requires a bachelor's-or-higher in a DIRECTLY RELATED specific specialty; not a specialty occupation if a general degree suffices. "Directly related" = a logical connection between degree and duties. Where multiple fields are listed, each must be directly related.
obligations.threshold: Required field must be a "specific specialty" directly related to duties; general-degree-sufficient = disqualifying. n/a numeric.
obligations.deadline: Adjudication (eligibility at filing; bona fide position as of requested start date).
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(ii); INA 214(i)(1) (8 USC 1184(i)(1)); "Modernizing H-1B Requirements" final rule, 89 FR 103054 (Dec 18, 2024), RIN 1615-AC70, eff. 01/17/2025.
obligations.data_needed: hSupp.q8_fieldsOfStudy[]; position.dutiesText; position.socCode; petition.degreeRequirement.

obligations.check: Wage offered/paid is at least the greater of the prevailing wage (at the certified level) and the actual wage.
obligations.requirement: Per 20 CFR 655.731, pay the required wage = greater of (a) the prevailing wage at the certified level, or (b) the actual wage to similarly employed workers with similar experience/qualifications. A higher offered wage can be justified by superior qualifications but must still meet the actual-wage test.
obligations.threshold: offeredWage ≥ max(prevailingWage_at_level, actualWage). Strict numeric.
obligations.deadline: For the entire period of authorized employment (attested at LCA filing; ongoing).
obligations.citation: 20 CFR 655.731(a) (first LCA requirement — required wage rate); INA 212(n)(1) (8 USC 1182(n)(1)).
obligations.data_needed: offer.wage; lca.prevailingWage; lca.wageLevel; lca.actualWage (employer pay data for similar workers); lca.areaOfEmployment; lca.socCode.
evidence_required: lca.actualWage (employer pay data for similar workers)

obligations.check: Stated minimum education (I-129 Q7) consistent with the LCA prevailing-wage LEVEL and the SOC/OEWS occupation.
obligations.requirement: Required education on the I-129 must be reconcilable with the certified LCA wage level. Under DOL methodology, an education requirement above the O*NET-SOC usual education adds wage-level step(s); a graduate-degree minimum is generally inconsistent with a Level I wage unless otherwise justified.
obligations.threshold: Education above the O*NET-SOC E&T/Appendix-D usual category = +1 step per category above (DOL Step 3). Flag when education-implied level > LCA wage level.
obligations.deadline: Evaluated at petition assembly / pre-filing audit; LCA must be certified before the I-129 is filed.
obligations.citation: DOL ETA Prevailing Wage Determination Policy Guidance (Nov-2009), Appendix A Step 3 (Education); 20 CFR 655.731; cross-ref 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A).
obligations.data_needed: hSupp.q7_educationLevelRequired; lca.wageLevel (I–IV); lca.socCode; soc.usualEducationCategory; lca.prevailingWageSource.

obligations.check: Stated minimum experience (I-129 Q9) consistent with the LCA wage level.
obligations.requirement: Required years of experience above the occupation's SVP/usual range push the level up (II/III). A multi-year experience minimum is generally inconsistent with a Level I wage.
obligations.threshold: Experience above the SVP range = +1 step (DOL Step 2). Heuristic: any required experience > 0 yrs paired with Level I; or experience materially above the typical entry range.
obligations.deadline: Pre-filing (LCA certified before I-129).
obligations.citation: DOL ETA PW Guidance (Nov-2009), Appendix A Step 2 (Experience); 20 CFR 655.731.
obligations.data_needed: hSupp.q9_yearsExperienceRequired; lca.wageLevel; lca.socCode; soc.svpRange.

obligations.check: Stated special skills (I-129 Q10) consistent with the LCA wage level.
obligations.requirement: Special skills/knowledge/licensure beyond entry-level add a step. Substantive special-skill requirements are generally inconsistent with a Level I wage.
obligations.threshold: Special skill/knowledge beyond normal entry = +1 step (DOL Step 4). Flag: non-empty special-skills requirement paired with Level I.
obligations.deadline: Pre-filing.
obligations.citation: DOL ETA PW Guidance (Nov-2009), Appendix A Step 4 (Special Skills, Knowledge, Licensure); 20 CFR 655.731.
obligations.data_needed: hSupp.q10_specialSkills; lca.wageLevel; lca.socCode; soc.entryLevelSkillBaseline.

obligations.check: Supervisory duties (I-129 Q11 > 0) reconciled with the LCA wage level WITHOUT auto-inflating to Level IV.
obligations.requirement: Supervision of >0 people adds one step — UNLESS supervision is a customary duty of the SOC (e.g., a First-Line Supervisor/Manager occupation), where no step is added. Supervisory duties do NOT automatically warrant Level IV.
obligations.threshold: Supervised count > 0 AND SOC not a First-Line-Supervisor/Manager occupation → +1 step (DOL Step 5). If SOC IS supervisory → +0.
obligations.deadline: Pre-filing.
obligations.citation: DOL ETA PW Guidance (Nov-2009), Appendix A Step 5 (Supervisory Duties); 20 CFR 655.731.
obligations.data_needed: hSupp.q11_numberSupervised; q11_supervisedTitles; lca.wageLevel; lca.socCode; soc.isSupervisoryOccupation (flag).

obligations.check: The beneficiary actually holds the qualification the position requires (degree/field/license/equivalency), matching Q7/Q8.
obligations.requirement: Per 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(C), the beneficiary must (1) hold the required U.S. bachelor's-or-higher from an accredited institution; or (2) an equivalent foreign degree; or (3) an unrestricted state license/registration/certification for full practice; or (4) education + specialized training and/or progressively responsible experience equivalent to the required U.S. degree, with recognized expertise. The degree field must match the directly-related field (Q8).
obligations.threshold: Beneficiary credential ≥ required degree level AND field within Q8 acceptable fields (or a documented (C)(2)/(C)(3)/(C)(4) equivalency). Experience equivalency: 3 yrs specialized experience per 1 year of missing college; for a Master's-equivalent, bachelor's + ≥5 yrs.
obligations.deadline: Eligibility as of filing.
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(C)(1)-(4) and (D) (equivalency, incl. the 3:1 ratio); INA 214(i)(2).
obligations.data_needed: beneficiary.degreeLevel; degreeField; institutionAccredited (bool); licenses[]; yearsRelevantExperience; hSupp.q7_educationLevelRequired; q8_fieldsOfStudy; evidence.credentialEvaluation.

obligations.check: The petitioner has a bona fide specialty-occupation position available for the beneficiary as of the requested start date.
obligations.requirement: Per 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(F) (added eff. 01/17/2025), at filing the petitioner must establish a bona fide specialty position available as of the requested validity start. Need not establish day-to-day assignments for the entire period, but must show non-speculative actual specialty work (esp. for third-party placement / staffing).
obligations.threshold: Bona fide position must exist as of the requested validity start. n/a numeric.
obligations.deadline: As of the requested validity-period start date; established at filing.
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(F); "Modernizing H-1B Requirements" final rule, 89 FR 103054 (Dec 18, 2024), eff. 01/17/2025.
obligations.data_needed: petition.requestedStartDate; evidence.workAvailability (SOW/work order/itinerary/project); placement.isThirdParty (bool); lca.worksites[].

obligations.check: If specialty status is asserted, the I-129 stated minimum education (Q7) is at least a bachelor's in the directly-related specialty.
obligations.requirement: An occupation qualifies only if it requires a bachelor's-or-higher in a directly related specific specialty as a minimum for entry. If the petitioner's own stated minimum (Q7/Q8) is less than a relevant bachelor's (or accepts a general/unrelated degree), the position is internally inconsistent with specialty-occupation status.
obligations.threshold: Q7 minimum ≥ U.S. bachelor's (or foreign equivalent) in a Q8 specialty field; less-than-bachelor's or "any field" = inconsistency.
obligations.deadline: Adjudication / pre-filing audit.
obligations.data_needed: hSupp.q7_educationLevelRequired; q8_fieldsOfStudy; petition.assertedSpecialty (bool); petition.degreeRequirement.

obligations.check: The position satisfies ≥1 of the four 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) specialty-occupation criteria, and the petition records which.
obligations.requirement: Must meet ≥1 of: (A)(1) a U.S. bachelor's-or-higher in a directly related specific specialty (or equivalent) is normally the minimum for entry; (A)(2) such a degree is normally required for parallel positions among similar organizations in the industry; (A)(3) the employer (or third party) normally requires such a degree for the duties; or (A)(4) the duties are so specialized, complex, or unique that the required knowledge is normally associated with such a degree.
obligations.threshold: ≥1 of 4 criteria. ((A)(1)/(A)(2) hinge on "normally"; (A)(3) on the employer's normal practice; (A)(4) on specialized/complex/unique duties.)
obligations.deadline: Adjudication (eligibility at filing; bona fide position as of requested start date).
obligations.data_needed: petition.assertedCriterion (1/2/3/4); position.dutiesText; position.socCode; evidence.industryDegreeNorm; evidence.employerNormalPractice; hSupp.q7_educationLevelRequired; q8_fieldsOfStudy.

obligations.check: SOC code and wage level consistent across the H-1B registration, the certified LCA, and the I-129 (incl. Q7–Q11) — no level-shopping or post-hoc downgrade.
obligations.requirement: Occupation (SOC), wage level, and position requirements must be coherent across registration, LCA (ETA-9035), and I-129. The LCA wage level cannot be "fixed" at the petition stage (no post-certification correction), so registration/LCA level must already match the I-129 position. A level inflated only to improve lottery odds, or a Level I selected to cut cost against a high-requirement role, is an inconsistency USCIS can now see directly.
obligations.threshold: SOC identical (or defensibly mapped) across all three; the I-129-requirements-implied level (DOL 4-factor mapping) must equal the certified LCA level. n/a single numeric.
obligations.deadline: Pre-filing (registration → LCA → I-129; reconcile before filing).
obligations.citation: 20 CFR 655.731 (required wage = greater of actual or prevailing); 8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A)/(E); DOL ETA PW Guidance (Nov-2009) level methodology.
obligations.data_needed: registration.socCode; registration.wageLevelProxy (if captured); lca.socCode; lca.wageLevel; lca.prevailingWage; lca.actualWage; hSupp.q7..q11; i129.socCode.

obligations.check: E-Verify case created by the third business day after the employee starts work for pay.
obligations.requirement: Create a case for each new hire no later than the 3rd business day after start of work for pay. Case cannot be created until the I-9 is complete; may not pre-screen before offer acceptance. Late cases require a documented delay reason.
obligations.threshold: By the 3rd business day after first day of work for pay. Earliest: after I-9 completion and offer acceptance.
obligations.deadline: 3rd business day after start of work for pay.
obligations.citation: E-Verify User Manual §2.2 "Create a Case"; prohibited-practices/pre-screening list + Glossary "Prescreening"; **FAR 52.222-54 (48 CFR 52.222-54), prescribed at FAR 22.1803** for federal contractors; E-Verify MOU Art. II.A (secondary). **REMOVE "6 CFR Part 5"** (that is DHS FOIA/Privacy Act disclosure, unrelated).
obligations.data_needed: first day of work for pay; eVerifyCaseCreationDate; i9CompletionDate; businessDayCalendar; delayReason (if late); federalContractorFlag.
evidence_required: first day of work for pay

obligations.check: Employer took NO adverse action against an employee contesting a TNC (case pending / referred / in continuance).
obligations.requirement: While a TNC case is pending (referred or in continuance), may not terminate, suspend, delay/withhold training, reduce hours, lower/withhold pay, or take any other adverse action because of the mismatch, until a Final Nonconfirmation. Employee continues working while resolving.
obligations.threshold: Zero adverse actions attributable to the mismatch until Final Nonconfirmation (or close with authorization).
obligations.deadline: n/a (prohibition spanning pendency).
obligations.citation: E-Verify MOU Art. II §A (paras 12-13, no-adverse-action / close-without-liability); E-Verify User Manual §3.3; 8 USC 1324b (anti-discrimination overlay: (a)(1) citizenship/national-origin + (a)(5) anti-retaliation).
obligations.data_needed: caseStatus timeline (TNC|referred|continuance|FNC|closed); adverse-action events (termination/suspension/hour-reduction/pay-change) with dates; reason codes.

obligations.check: Photo-matching step performed and, on a photo-mismatch contest, a copy of the employee's document submitted to DHS.
obligations.requirement: For photo-matching documents (U.S. passport/passport card, Form I-551, Form I-766), compare the E-Verify-displayed photo to the document photo and indicate match. On a contested DHS photo-mismatch TNC, attach/submit a copy of the document to DHS.
obligations.threshold: Photo comparison recorded; on photo-mismatch contest, document copy uploaded to DHS.
obligations.deadline: Case created by the 3rd business day after start of work for pay; employer notify+refer within 10 federal working days of mismatch; employee acts within 8 federal working days after referral. *(Original "10 federal working days to act" conflated the employer's 10-day window with the employee's separate 8-day window.)*
obligations.citation: E-Verify User Manual §2.2.2 (E-Verify Photo Matching) and §3.3 (TNC handling); E-Verify MOU Art. II.
obligations.data_needed: section2DocType; photoMatchResult (match|no-match|recorded); on photo-TNC contest: documentCopySubmittedToDHS (bool); copyRetained (bool).

obligations.check: Referred employee given the 8-federal-working-day window to contact SSA/DHS, reflected in the Referral Date Confirmation.
obligations.requirement: On a contested+referred TNC, the employee must contact DHS or visit an SSA field office within 8 federal government working days; employer must print and give the Referral Date Confirmation (read/translate if LEP) and attach a copy to the I-9.
obligations.threshold: Employee has 8 federal government working days from referral; employer must provide the Referral Date Confirmation.
obligations.deadline: 8 federal government working days for the employee (employer duty: provide the confirmation at referral).
obligations.citation: **E-Verify User Manual §3.3.3 "Refer Employee To DHS or SSA"** (with §3.3.2 "Confirm Employee Decision" as cross-ref); E-Verify MOU Art. II. **The supplied §3.3.2 URL/slug is stale/dead** (manual renamed "tnc" → "mismatch").
obligations.data_needed: referralDate; referralDateConfirmationProvided (bool); federalWorkingDayCalendar.

obligations.check: On a TNC (mismatch), employer notified the employee promptly and completed required referral steps within 10 federal government working days.
obligations.requirement: Notify the employee ASAP, give and privately review the Further Action Notice (FAN), let the employee decide, confirm the decision, and refer if contested — all within 10 federal government working days of mismatch issuance. If no decision by day 10, close the case.
obligations.threshold: Employer action (notify + confirm decision + refer if contested) within 10 federal government working days of TNC issuance.
obligations.deadline: 10 federal government working days after TNC issuance.
obligations.citation: E-Verify MOU Art. II §A; E-Verify User Manual §3.3 (incl. 3.3.1 Notify / 3.3.2 Confirm Decision / 3.3.3 Refer); USCIS guidance "REMINDER: Employer Action Required on Tentative Nonconfirmations (Mismatches) within 10 Federal Government Working Days."
obligations.data_needed: tncIssueDate; employeeNotifiedDate; fanGivenDate; employeeDecisionDate; referralDate; federalWorkingDayCalendar.

obligations.check: Referred employee given the 8-federal-working-day window to contact SSA/DHS, reflected in the Referral Date Confirmation.
obligations.requirement: On a contested+referred TNC, the employee must contact DHS or visit an SSA field office within 8 federal government working days; employer must print and give the Referral Date Confirmation (read/translate if LEP) and attach a copy to the I-9.
obligations.threshold: Employee has 8 federal government working days from referral; employer must provide the Referral Date Confirmation.
obligations.deadline: 8 federal government working days for the employee (employer duty: provide the confirmation at referral).
obligations.citation: **E-Verify User Manual §3.3.3 "Refer Employee To DHS or SSA"** (with §3.3.2 "Confirm Employee Decision" as cross-ref); E-Verify MOU Art. II. **The supplied §3.3.2 URL/slug is stale/dead** (manual renamed "tnc" → "mismatch").
obligations.data_needed: referralDate; referralDateConfirmationProvided (bool); federalWorkingDayCalendar.

obligations.check: Awareness that 1324b charges must be filed with DOJ-IER within 180 days of the act.
obligations.requirement: A charge of an unfair immigration-related employment practice must be filed with DOJ-IER within 180 days of the alleged occurrence.
obligations.threshold: 180 days from the act.
obligations.deadline: 180 days after the act.
obligations.data_needed: date of alleged act; date charge filed (if known).

obligations.check: No citizenship-status or national-origin discrimination in hiring, firing, or recruitment/referral for a fee.
obligations.requirement: Unlawful to intentionally discriminate against protected individuals by citizenship/immigration status, or any individual by national origin, in hiring/discharge/recruitment-or-referral-for-a-fee. National-origin coverage under 1324b: employers with 4–14 employees (Title VII covers 15+; citizenship-status prong has no upper cap and binds all 4+). "US-citizen-only" policies generally unlawful absent a law/contract requirement.
obligations.threshold: No intentional citizenship-status/national-origin discrimination; "US-citizen-only" unlawful unless required by law/regulation/EO/government contract (INA 274B(a)(2)(C)).
obligations.deadline: Charge filed with DOJ-IER within 180 days of the act.
obligations.citation: 8 USC 1324b(a)(1),(a)(2),(a)(3); 28 CFR 44.200; penalties 8 USC 1324b(g)(2)(B)(iv)(I)-(III) as adjusted in 28 CFR 85.5. Sharpen: 180-day deadline = **1324b(d)(3)**; the "4–14" band is a synthesis of **(a)(2)(A)** (floor: excludes "three or fewer," so 4+) and **(a)(2)(B)** (ceiling: national-origin deferred to Title VII, so 15+) — not verbatim statutory text.
obligations.data_needed: employee count (for the 4–14 national-origin line); job-posting citizenship requirements; legal/contractual basis for any citizenship requirement; adverse-action records by protected status.
evidence_required: legal/contractual basis for any citizenship requirement

obligations.check: Employer did not request more/different documents than required, or specify which documents the employee must present.
obligations.requirement: Must not request more/different docs, specify which acceptable doc(s) to present, or reject genuine-appearing docs — when done with intent to discriminate by citizenship status or national origin ("document abuse" / unfair documentary practices).
obligations.threshold: No over/under-documentation; employee free choice; no document-type targeting by citizenship/national origin. **Intent to discriminate required.**
obligations.deadline: n/a (charge filed with DOJ-IER within 180 days — see charge_window).
obligations.citation: 8 USC 1324b(a)(1) & (a)(6); 28 CFR 44.200(a)(3); penalty 8 USC 1324b(g)(2)(B)(iv)(IV) as adjusted in 28 CFR 85.5.
obligations.data_needed: per form: documents-per-list count (over-collection = List A + B/C both present); doc type vs national-origin/citizenship status (risk signal only); rejection events.
evidence_required: per form: documents-per-list count (over-collection = List A + B/C both present)
doc type vs national-origin/citizenship status (risk signal only)

obligations.check: Corrections by line-through + initial + date; no white-out, no backdating; written explanation; correct party corrects each section.
obligations.requirement: Draw a single line through the error, enter correct info, initial and date. Never erase/white-out. Never backdate (enter current date + initial). Attach a dated written explanation (signature recommended). Employee corrects Section 1; employer corrects Section 2.
obligations.threshold: Line-through + initials + correction date; no white-out; no backdated entries; explanation attached.
obligations.deadline: n/a (governs how, not when).
obligations.citation: **M-274 §9.0 (Correcting Errors or Missing Information on Form I-9)** — the governing source; optionally **Form I-9 Instructions**. **DROP "8 CFR 274a.2(b)(2) (integrity of the record)"** — (b)(2) is the retention rule; no paragraph of 274a.2 prescribes manual line-through/initial/date corrections (that procedure exists only in M-274 §9.0).
obligations.data_needed: correctionEvents: field changed, who corrected, correctionDate vs originalDate, method (line-through|whiteout|overwrite), explanationAttached (bool).

obligations.check: Only currently-acceptable List A/B/C documents accepted in the correct combination.
obligations.requirement: Identity + employment authorization established only by docs on the current Lists of Acceptable Documents: List A = both; List B = identity only; List C = employment auth only. List A stands alone; otherwise one List B AND one List C. Don't ask for more from someone presenting an acceptable List A doc.
obligations.threshold: {one List A} XOR {one List B + one List C}; on current list; unexpired (except no-expiry docs).
obligations.deadline: At Section 2 / reverification.
obligations.data_needed: canonical DOC_CATALOG tagged List A/B/C with hasExpiry + acceptability window; per-form recorded doc types + numbers + expiries; reverification docs (List A or C only).
evidence_required: canonical DOC_CATALOG tagged List A/B/C with hasExpiry + acceptability window
per-form recorded doc types + numbers + expiries
reverification docs (List A or C only)

obligations.check: Employer used a Form I-9 edition that was current/accepted when any part of the form was initially completed.
obligations.requirement: Failure to use a version of Form I-9 that is current at the time any part of the form is initially completed is a technical/procedural failure under the ICE I-9 Inspection fact sheet. If ICE serves a Notice of Technical or Procedural Failures, the employer receives at least 10 business days to correct; uncorrected technical failures become substantive.
obligations.threshold: `formEditionDate` must be in the USCIS accepted-editions table on the initial completion date. If no edition date can be extracted, return `insufficient_evidence`, not compliant.
obligations.deadline: At initial Form I-9 completion; cure clock only starts if ICE issues a technical/procedural-failure notice.
obligations.citation: ICE Form I-9 Inspection fact sheet updated 2026-03-16 (technical failures list); current form/edition source = USCIS Form I-9 page + M-274; cure period = 8 USC 1324a(b)(6).
obligations.data_needed: formEditionDate; initialCompletionDate; acceptedI9EditionTable with effective/expiration dates; correctionDate if later cured.

obligations.check: Paperwork penalty derived from the five statutory factors and the correct per-form base range.
obligations.requirement: Per-individual penalty set within the range using FIVE factors: (1) business size, (2) good faith, (3) seriousness, (4) whether the individual was an unauthorized alien, (5) prior-violation history. ICE's baseline-percentage matrix scales within the min/max; OCAHO may adjust.
obligations.threshold: Per individual/form: $288–$2,861 (2025, in force through CY2026). Knowing-hire separate: 1st $716–$5,724; 2nd $5,724–$14,308; 3rd+ $8,586–$28,619. Indemnity-bond: $2,861.
obligations.deadline: n/a.
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2) (paperwork + five factors) and (b)(1)(ii)(A)-(C) (knowing-hire tiers); inflation-adjusted amounts 28 CFR 85.5; 8 USC 1324a(e)(5),(e)(4).
obligations.data_needed: employer size; good-faith indicators; per-violation seriousness tag; unauthorized-alien status; prior-violation history; violationDate + assessmentDate.

obligations.check: No citizenship-status or national-origin discrimination in hiring, firing, or recruitment/referral for a fee.
obligations.requirement: Unlawful to intentionally discriminate against protected individuals by citizenship/immigration status, or any individual by national origin, in hiring/discharge/recruitment-or-referral-for-a-fee. National-origin coverage under 1324b: employers with 4–14 employees (Title VII covers 15+; citizenship-status prong has no upper cap and binds all 4+). "US-citizen-only" policies generally unlawful absent a law/contract requirement.
obligations.threshold: No intentional citizenship-status/national-origin discrimination; "US-citizen-only" unlawful unless required by law/regulation/EO/government contract (INA 274B(a)(2)(C)).
obligations.deadline: Charge filed with DOJ-IER within 180 days of the act.
obligations.citation: 8 USC 1324b(a)(1),(a)(2),(a)(3); 28 CFR 44.200; penalties 8 USC 1324b(g)(2)(B)(iv)(I)-(III) as adjusted in 28 CFR 85.5. Sharpen: 180-day deadline = **1324b(d)(3)**; the "4–14" band is a synthesis of **(a)(2)(A)** (floor: excludes "three or fewer," so 4+) and **(a)(2)(B)** (ceiling: national-origin deferred to Title VII, so 15+) — not verbatim statutory text.
obligations.data_needed: employee count (for the 4–14 national-origin line); job-posting citizenship requirements; legal/contractual basis for any citizenship requirement; adverse-action records by protected status.
evidence_required: legal/contractual basis for any citizenship requirement

obligations.check: Employer did not request more/different documents than required, or specify which documents the employee must present.
obligations.requirement: Must not request more/different docs, specify which acceptable doc(s) to present, or reject genuine-appearing docs — when done with intent to discriminate by citizenship status or national origin ("document abuse" / unfair documentary practices).
obligations.threshold: No over/under-documentation; employee free choice; no document-type targeting by citizenship/national origin. **Intent to discriminate required.**
obligations.deadline: n/a (charge filed with DOJ-IER within 180 days — see charge_window).
obligations.citation: 8 USC 1324b(a)(1) & (a)(6); 28 CFR 44.200(a)(3); penalty 8 USC 1324b(g)(2)(B)(iv)(IV) as adjusted in 28 CFR 85.5.
obligations.data_needed: per form: documents-per-list count (over-collection = List A + B/C both present); doc type vs national-origin/citizenship status (risk signal only); rejection events.
evidence_required: per form: documents-per-list count (over-collection = List A + B/C both present)
doc type vs national-origin/citizenship status (risk signal only)

obligations.check: Receipt for a lost/stolen/damaged document handled within the receipt rule and replaced within 90 days.
obligations.requirement: Accept a receipt for the replacement application; employee presents the actual replacement within 90 days of hire (or, for reverification, within 90 days of the work-auth expiry). Receipt rule unavailable for <3-business-day engagements. Distinct arrival-document and refugee receipts have their own windows.
obligations.threshold: Replacement presented within 90 days of hire (or reverification trigger). Receipt rule unavailable for <3-day hires.
obligations.deadline: 90 days from hire (or reverification date).
obligations.citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(vi)(A)** (lost/stolen/damaged receipt + 90-day replacement); short-term <3-day exception **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(iii)** (also restated in (b)(1)(vi)); **distinct arrival-document and refugee receipts at 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(vi)(B) and (b)(1)(vi)(C)** — NOT (b)(1)(iii); **M-274 §4.4**.
obligations.data_needed: receiptUsed (bool); receiptType; hireDate (or reverification date); replacementDocPresentedDate; employmentDurationDays.

obligations.check: Rehire handled correctly via Supplement B when rehiring within 3 years of original I-9 execution.
obligations.requirement: If rehired within 3 years of the date the original I-9 was executed, employer may either complete a new I-9 or complete Supplement B (recording rehire date and reverifying if prior authorization expired).
obligations.threshold: Within 3 years of original I-9 → Supplement B permitted; beyond 3 years → new I-9 required.
obligations.deadline: By the rehire date (and within Section 2 / reverification timing if a new auth check is needed).
obligations.citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(c)(1)** (rehire within 3 years of initial I-9 execution; reverify expired authorization per (b)(1)(vii)); **USCIS M-274 §6.0 / §6.2**. **DROP the "(b)(1)(viii)-(ix)" pinpoint** — (b)(1)(viii) = continuing employment (leave/layoff/promotion); (b)(1)(ix) = alternative document-examination procedures; neither addresses rehire.
obligations.data_needed: originalI9Date (= the Section-2 execution date); rehireDate; priorWorkAuthExpiry; whether new I-9 or Supplement B used on rehire.
evidence_required: whether new I-9 or Supplement B used on rehire

obligations.check: Remote (alternative-procedure) exam used only by qualified E-Verify employers, with the box checked and copies retained.
obligations.requirement: Examine documents remotely only if enrolled in E-Verify in good standing (and, for the employee, created an E-Verify case except for reverification): examine front-and-back copies, conduct a LIVE video interaction, CHECK the alternative-procedure box in Section 2/Supplement B, and RETAIN clear/legible front-and-back copies.
obligations.threshold: E-Verify enrolled + good standing + case created (non-reverification) + live video + box checked + copies retained.
obligations.deadline: Same 3-business-day Section 2 clock.
obligations.citation: **DHS final rule "Optional Alternatives to the Physical Document Examination," 88 FR 47990 (publ. July 25, 2023; eff. Aug 1, 2023)** — added **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ix)**; companion authorization notice **"Optional Alternative 1," 88 FR 47749 (July 25, 2023)** (sets out the five operative conditions); **M-274 §4.5**; 3-day clock **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii)**.
obligations.data_needed: remoteAlternativeUsed (bool); employerEnrolledInEVerify + goodStanding; eVerifyCaseCreated (except reverification); altProcedureBoxChecked; copiesRetainedFrontBack; liveVideoConducted (attested).

obligations.check: Form I-9 retained for the later of 3 years from hire OR 1 year from termination.
obligations.requirement: Retain each I-9 until the LATER of (a) 3 years after hire, or (b) 1 year after termination.
obligations.threshold: Retain until max(hireDate + 3y, terminationDate + 1y). Active employees: indefinitely.
obligations.deadline: Earliest destruction date = max(hire+3y, term+1y).
obligations.data_needed: hireDate; terminationDate (nullable); i9OnFile (bool); destructionDate if purged.

obligations.check: I-9s stored in a compliant medium and producible within 3 business days of an inspection request.
obligations.requirement: Retain on paper (original signatures), microfilm/microfiche (reader-printer at exam site), or electronically (access controls, backup/recovery, training, secure-permanent-record audit trail on create/complete/update/modify/alter/correct). Produce within 3 business days of an inspection request.
obligations.threshold: Production within 3 business days; electronic systems meet the security/audit-trail standard.
obligations.deadline: 3 business days after NOI / inspection request.
obligations.citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(2)(i)-(ii)** (retention period + 3-business-days inspection notice / production-at-location) — *not* (b)(3), which is "Copying of documentation"; **8 CFR 274a.2(e)-(g)** (electronic retention standards: (e) controls/indexing, (f) documentation/audit trails, (g) security incl. (g)(1)(iv) secure-permanent-record-on-create/complete/update/modify/alter/correct); **M-274 §10.0–10.1** ("present within 3 business days of the date requested").
obligations.data_needed: storageMedium (paper|microfilm|electronic); for electronic: accessControls, backup, auditTrail, tamperEvident (bools); inspectionProducibility / time-to-produce.

obligations.check: Reverification (Supplement B) completed on/before the date the employee's temporary work authorization expires.
obligations.requirement: When recorded employment authorization (or the document evidencing it) has an expiration date, reverify continued authorization in Supplement B no later than the expiry, examining a List A or List C doc the employee chooses.
obligations.threshold: Reverification recorded on/before the work-authorization expiration date.
obligations.deadline: By the expiry date of the employment authorization.
obligations.citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(vii)**; paperwork penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2)**; knowing-continued-employment penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(1)** (use **(b)(1)(i)** for first-offense tier — (b)(1)(ii) is the *second*-offense tier, $5,724–$14,308).
obligations.data_needed: workAuthExpiry; reverificationDate (Supplement B); reverifiedDocType; current employment status.

obligations.check: Employer did NOT improperly reverify documents/persons on the no-reverify list.
obligations.requirement: Never reverify on expiry of: U.S. passport, U.S. passport card, Form I-551 (green card); never reverify List B (identity-only) docs; never reverify U.S. citizens/noncitizen nationals/LPRs. Demanding such reverification can be unlawful document abuse.
obligations.threshold: No reverification demanded based on expiry of US passport/passport card/Form I-551, a List B doc, or for a US citizen/national/LPR.
obligations.deadline: n/a (prohibition).
obligations.data_needed: recorded Section-2 doc type; Section-1 status attested; reverification events + the doc type that triggered them.
evidence_required: reverification events + the doc type that triggered them

obligations.check: Reverification (Supplement B) completed on/before the date the employee's temporary work authorization expires.
obligations.requirement: When recorded employment authorization (or the document evidencing it) has an expiration date, reverify continued authorization in Supplement B no later than the expiry, examining a List A or List C doc the employee chooses.
obligations.threshold: Reverification recorded on/before the work-authorization expiration date.
obligations.deadline: By the expiry date of the employment authorization.
obligations.citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(vii)**; paperwork penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2)**; knowing-continued-employment penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(1)** (use **(b)(1)(i)** for first-offense tier — (b)(1)(ii) is the *second*-offense tier, $5,724–$14,308).
obligations.data_needed: workAuthExpiry; reverificationDate (Supplement B); reverifiedDocType; current employment status.

obligations.check: No citizenship-status or national-origin discrimination in hiring, firing, or recruitment/referral for a fee.
obligations.requirement: Unlawful to intentionally discriminate against protected individuals by citizenship/immigration status, or any individual by national origin, in hiring/discharge/recruitment-or-referral-for-a-fee. National-origin coverage under 1324b: employers with 4–14 employees (Title VII covers 15+; citizenship-status prong has no upper cap and binds all 4+). "US-citizen-only" policies generally unlawful absent a law/contract requirement.
obligations.threshold: No intentional citizenship-status/national-origin discrimination; "US-citizen-only" unlawful unless required by law/regulation/EO/government contract (INA 274B(a)(2)(C)).
obligations.deadline: Charge filed with DOJ-IER within 180 days of the act.
obligations.citation: 8 USC 1324b(a)(1),(a)(2),(a)(3); 28 CFR 44.200; penalties 8 USC 1324b(g)(2)(B)(iv)(I)-(III) as adjusted in 28 CFR 85.5. Sharpen: 180-day deadline = **1324b(d)(3)**; the "4–14" band is a synthesis of **(a)(2)(A)** (floor: excludes "three or fewer," so 4+) and **(a)(2)(B)** (ceiling: national-origin deferred to Title VII, so 15+) — not verbatim statutory text.
obligations.data_needed: employee count (for the 4–14 national-origin line); job-posting citizenship requirements; legal/contractual basis for any citizenship requirement; adverse-action records by protected status.
evidence_required: legal/contractual basis for any citizenship requirement

obligations.check: Section 1 attestation signed AND dated by the employee.
obligations.requirement: Employee signs and dates the Section 1 attestation under penalty of perjury. Preparer/translator who assisted completes Supplement A.
obligations.threshold: Employee signature present AND date present.
obligations.deadline: Day 1 of employment ("at the time of hire").
obligations.citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(i)(A)** (completes Section 1 "at the time of hire" and signs the attestation; preparer/translator assistance clause is in this same subparagraph) + **8 CFR 274a.2(a)(3)** (attestation "under penalty of perjury"). Deadline = "at the time of hire" per **8 CFR 274a.1(g)**, operationally end of first day per M-274. The DATE-field requirement derives from the **Form I-9 instructions / M-274**, not the reg. **DROP 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(2)** (that is the retention rule) and **DROP the Virtue Memo as authority for the signature mandate** (it governs the technical-vs-substantive classification only). Preparer/Translator = **Supplement A** (current Form I-9, 08/01/2023).
obligations.data_needed: section1SignaturePresent (bool); section1SignDate.

obligations.check: Employee checked exactly one of the four citizenship/immigration-status attestation boxes in Section 1.
obligations.requirement: Employee attests to exactly one of: (1) U.S. citizen; (2) noncitizen national; (3) LPR (with A-number/USCIS number); (4) noncitizen authorized to work (with work-auth expiry if applicable + A-number/USCIS number, I-94 number, or foreign passport number).
obligations.threshold: Exactly one of four boxes; zero or multiple = defect.
obligations.deadline: At Section 1 completion (day 1).
obligations.citation: The four-box "check exactly one" rule lives on the **Form I-9 (ed. 01/20/25)** + **USCIS Form I-9 Instructions (01/20/25)** + **M-274 §3.0** — NOT in the reg. Regulatory duty to complete Section 1 + sign: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(i)(A)**. Substantive/non-curable classification: **ICE Form I-9 Inspection fact sheet updated 2026-03-16**. Penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2)**.
obligations.data_needed: section1StatusAttested enum (citizen|national|lpr|alien_authorized|none); boxesCheckedCount; for LPR: aNumber; for alien_authorized: workAuthExpiry + one of (aNumber|i94|foreignPassport).

obligations.check: Section 1 completed and signed by the employee on/before the first day of employment for pay.
obligations.requirement: Employee completes and signs Section 1 (Employee Information and Attestation) at the time of hire = actual commencement of employment for wages. May be done after offer acceptance, never before. <3-business-day engagements: by day 1.
obligations.threshold: By end of business on day 1 (first day worked for pay); not before offer acceptance.
obligations.deadline: First day of employment (hire date). No grace.
obligations.citation: Regulatory hook **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(i)(A)** ("Completes section 1 … at the time of hire and signs the attestation") + **8 CFR 274a.1** (definition of "hire" = "the actual commencement of employment … for wages or other remuneration"). The "first day of employment / after offer / not before offer" gloss is **USCIS M-274 §3.0 / Form I-9 Instructions**, not the CFR. Penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2)** / **8 USC 1324a(e)(5)**.
obligations.data_needed: employeeId; hireDate (first day of employment for pay); section1CompletedDate; section1SignedFlag; section1SignDate; offerAcceptedDate.
evidence_required: hireDate (first day of employment for pay)

obligations.check: Employer signed and dated the Section 2 attestation.
obligations.requirement: Employer/authorized rep signs and dates Section 2, certifying under penalty of perjury that it examined the documents and they appear genuine and relate to the employee.
obligations.threshold: Employer signature present AND date present.
obligations.deadline: Within 3 business days of hire.
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii); ICE Form I-9 Inspection fact sheet updated 2026-03-16; penalty 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2).
obligations.data_needed: section2EmployerSignaturePresent (bool); section2EmployerSignDate.

obligations.check: Employer physically (or via authorized remote alternative) examined original documents that reasonably appear genuine and relate to the person.
obligations.requirement: Examine original document(s) (or copies + live video under the DHS remote alternative for qualified E-Verify employers); ensure they reasonably appear genuine and relate to the individual. Employee — not employer — chooses List A vs List B+C.
obligations.threshold: One List A doc, OR one List B (identity) + one List C (employment auth). Reasonable-appearance standard.
obligations.deadline: Within 3 business days of hire.
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii)(A); 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(v); remote alt 88 FR 47990 (publ. **July 25, 2023**; eff. Aug 1, 2023) / M-274 §4.5. Optional precision: cite **274a.2(b)(1)(ix)** (remote-alternative authority) and **274a.2(a)(2) / INA 274B (8 USC 1324b)** (employee-choice / anti-over-documentation).
obligations.data_needed: listA docs OR (listB + listC); per doc: title, issuing authority, number, expiration; remoteAlternativeUsed (bool); copiesRetained (bool, required if remote).

obligations.check: Section 2 records document title, issuing authority, document number, expiration date per document, plus the employee's first day of employment.
obligations.requirement: Record for each document: title, issuing authority, number, expiration (if any); record first day of employment; sign and date the employer attestation with business name/address.
obligations.threshold: All required fields populated; employer signature + date + business name/address.
obligations.deadline: Within 3 business days of hire.
obligations.citation: **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii)** (within 3 business days; physically examine; complete Section 2 + sign) AND **8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(v)** ("The identification number and expiration date … of all documents must be noted … on the Form I-9"). **Document title and issuing authority fields derive from the Form I-9 itself / M-274**, not the CFR text. Penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2)**.
obligations.data_needed: per doc: title, issuingAuthority, number, expiration (nullable for non-expiring docs); section2EmployerSignature + date; businessName; businessAddress; firstDayOfEmployment; copiesRetainedEvidenceFlag (evidence only, not severity-changing).

obligations.check: Section 2 completed within 3 business days of the first day of employment.
obligations.requirement: Within 3 business days of hire, employer (or authorized rep) physically examines documents and completes Section 2. <3-business-day engagements: Section 2 at time of hire (day 1).
obligations.threshold: 3 business days; first day of employment = day 0, due by end of 3rd business day after. Weekends + federal holidays excluded.
obligations.deadline: End of the 3rd business day after the first day of employment.
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii); short-engagement exception 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(iii); penalty 8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2).
obligations.data_needed: hire/start date; section2CompletionDate (employer sign date); businessDayCalendar (federal holidays); employmentDurationDays.

obligations.check: Preparer/translator certification (Supplement A) completed when someone assisted the employee with Section 1.
obligations.requirement: Each assisting preparer/translator completes a separate Preparer and/or Translator Certification block in Supplement A, signs and dates it. Employee must still personally sign Section 1.
obligations.threshold: Supplement A present and signed for each assisting preparer/translator.
obligations.deadline: Same time as Section 1 (day 1).
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(i)(A); M-274 Supplement A guidance.
obligations.data_needed: preparerUsed (bool, often not captured); supplementAPresent (bool); supplementASignature + date.

obligations.check: Classify each defect as substantive vs technical/procedural and apply the ≥10-business-day cure period correctly.
obligations.requirement: During an ICE I-9 inspection, technical/procedural failures are noted on a Notice of Technical or Procedural Failures with AT LEAST 10 business days to correct; uncorrected → substantive. Substantive + uncorrected-technical violations are penalized.
obligations.threshold: Substantive = no cure. Technical/procedural = ≥10 business days to cure; uncorrected → substantive. Cure period runs from ICE's notice.
obligations.deadline: ≥10 business days from the Notice of Technical or Procedural Failures.
obligations.citation: Cure provision = **INA 274A(b)(6) = 8 USC 1324a(b)(6)** ("not less than 10 business days") — **NOT 8 CFR 274a.2(b)(3)** (the cure period is statutory and does not appear in 274a.2). Penalty **8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2)** (correct). **The 1997 Virtue Memorandum no longer controls the classification** — superseded by the **ICE Form I-9 Inspection fact sheet updated 2026-03-16**. Current substantive examples include missing Section 1 date/signature/status, missing Section 2 document title/issuing authority/number/expiration, missing alternative-procedure checkbox where applicable, and missing Section 2 signature/date.
obligations.data_needed: per defect: defect type; section; prepared/presented flags; timeliness facts; cure status + cure date vs ICE notice date; retained-copy evidence may be captured for record completeness but must not lower severity.
evidence_required: cure status + cure date vs ICE notice date
retained-copy evidence may be captured for record completeness but must not lowe

obligations.check: The beneficiary's admission / I-94 period does not exceed the petition (or blanket) validity, and status is maintained within it.
obligations.requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(11): apply for admission only while the petition is valid; an individual-petition beneficiary "shall not be admitted for a date past the validity period"; a blanket beneficiary may be admitted for 3 years even if the blanket's initial validity expires sooner. Admission "shall not exceed three years unless an extension … is granted." Under 8 CFR 214.1(l)(1), admitted for validity + up to 10 days before/after, but may not work except during validity.
obligations.threshold: Admission/I-94 end ≤ petition validity end (individual) or ≤3 years (blanket). +10/−10 day grace bracket (no work in those days). Single admission generally ≤3 years.
obligations.deadline: Status ends at I-94 expiry; extensions must be timely filed (before expiry).
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(11); 8 CFR 214.1(l)(1)-(2) (period of stay / 10-day brackets / 60-day grace on cessation); (l)(7)(i)(A)(2).
obligations.data_needed: i94_admit_until_date; petition_validity_end; blanket_flag; current_date; work_start_date; work_end_date; grace_period_flag; cessation_of_employment_date.

obligations.check: An amended L-1 petition is filed on a material change in the approved relationship, employment capacity, or other eligibility fact.
obligations.requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(7)(i)(C): file an amended petition (with fee) at the office where the original was filed "to reflect changes in approved relationships, additional qualifying organizations under a blanket petition, change in capacity of employment (i.e., from a specialized knowledge position to a managerial position), or any information which would affect the beneficiary's eligibility under section 101(a)(15)(L)."
obligations.threshold: Materiality = any change affecting the approved relationship, capacity, or eligibility under INA 101(a)(15)(L). (A work-location change performing the same duties for the same employer is generally NOT, by itself, material — but fact-dependent.)
obligations.deadline: When the material change occurs / before the changed employment begins (no fixed numeric clock; unlike H-1B Simeio).
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(7)(i)(C); (l)(9)(iii)(A) (revocation grounds); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L.
obligations.data_needed: change_event_type (relationship|blanket_entity|capacity|worksite|duties|salary|other); change_date; amended_petition_filed_flag; amended_petition_filed_date; new_capacity; new_worksite; duties_changed_flag.

obligations.check: A blanket L petition meets all four blanket-eligibility thresholds.
obligations.requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(4)(i): file a blanket only if (A) petitioner and each listed entity are engaged in commercial trade or services; (B) the petitioner has a U.S. office doing business for ≥1 year; (C) ≥3 domestic and foreign branches/subsidiaries/affiliates; AND (D) either ≥10 "L" managers/execs/SK-professionals approved in the previous 12 months, OR U.S. subsidiaries/affiliates with combined annual sales ≥$25 million, OR a U.S. workforce ≥1,000 employees.
obligations.threshold: U.S. office ≥1 year; ≥3 entities; AND (≥10 L approvals in prior 12 months OR ≥$25,000,000 combined U.S. annual sales OR ≥1,000 U.S. employees).
obligations.deadline: Blanket initial validity 3 years ((l)(7)(i)(B)(2)), extendible indefinitely if compliant.
obligations.data_needed: blanket_flag; commercial_trade_or_services_flag_all_entities; us_office_doing_business_years; count_branches_subs_affiliates; count_L_approvals_prior_12mo; combined_us_annual_sales; us_employee_count.

obligations.check: Each beneficiary entering under an approved blanket uses a properly completed Form I-129S and the consular/admission documents are valid and within time limits.
obligations.requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(5): complete Form I-129S (original + three copies), attach a copy of the approved I-797, retain one copy, send the original + two copies to the alien; the employee "may use these documents to apply for visa issuance … within six months of the date on Form I-129S." The consular/Service officer determines mgr/exec/SK-professional. The I-129S is stamped for ≤3 years. Eligibility under a blanket is limited to managers, executives, and SK PROFESSIONALS (the professional requirement of (l)(1)(ii)(E) applies to blanket SK).
obligations.threshold: I-129S used within 6 months of the date on the form; blanket admission/validity ≤3 years; SK beneficiaries under a blanket must be professionals (degree-level).
obligations.deadline: 6 months from the I-129S date to apply for the visa; admission ≤ validity.
obligations.data_needed: blanket_flag; i129s_present_flag; i129s_date; visa_application_date; i797_blanket_copy_flag; beneficiary_capacity (mgr|exec|SK_professional); is_professional_flag (degree per INA 101(a)(32)); admission_validity_end.

obligations.check: L-1 dual intent is respected (pending PERM/I-140/I-485 is not a denial basis); L-2 dependents properly classified and (spouse) work-authorized.
obligations.requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(16): an alien may legitimately come as L-1 and simultaneously lawfully seek permanent residence; the filing of a PERM, immigrant visa preference petition, or AOS "shall not be the basis for denying" an L-1 petition/extension/admission or related COS. (l)(7)(ii): the spouse and unmarried minor children get L-2 for the same period/limits; per INA 214(c)(2)(E) the L-2 spouse is authorized to work (incident to status).
obligations.threshold: Dual intent permitted (no denial solely on immigrant intent). L-2 spouse work-authorized; L-2 children may NOT work. Dependents' stay tied to the principal's period/limits.
obligations.deadline: n/a (status condition).
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(16) (dual intent); (l)(7)(ii) (spouse/dependents); INA 214(c)(2)(E) (8 USC 1184(c)(2)(E)) (L-2 spouse employment); 8 CFR 274a.12(a) (L-2 spouse employment incident to status).
obligations.data_needed: pending_perm_or_i140_or_i485_flag; dependent_records (relationship: spouse|child); dependent_status (L-2); l2_spouse_employment_flag; child_age; child_marital_status; dependent_admit_until_date.

obligations.check: Extension of stay (and concurrent petition extension) filed before the current authorized stay expires, increments within caps.
obligations.requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(15)(i): for individual petitions, apply for the petition extension and the alien's EOS concurrently on Form I-129. For a blanket beneficiary, file a new Certificate of Eligibility + a copy of the prior approved certificate; the dates must be the same for petition and EOS. The beneficiary must be physically present in the U.S. at filing. (l)(14)(i): an individual extension may be filed only if the original validity has not expired. (l)(15)(ii): EOS in ≤2-year increments, ≤5/7 years.
obligations.threshold: File before original validity expires; beneficiary physically present at filing; increments ≤2 years; cumulative ≤5/7 years.
obligations.deadline: Before the original petition's validity expires (a late extension cannot be filed on an expired petition).
obligations.data_needed: original_petition_validity_end; extension_filing_date; beneficiary_physically_present_us_flag; requested_increment; cumulative_l_time; classification (L-1A|L-1B).

obligations.check: No fraud or willful material misrepresentation in the L petition / supporting evidence (statement of facts true and correct).
obligations.requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(9)(iii)(A)(4) makes a petition revocable where the statement of facts "was not true and correct." INA 212(a)(6)(C)(i): an alien who by fraud or willfully misrepresenting a material fact seeks/procures a visa/admission/benefit is inadmissible. Material if, had the truth been known, the alien would not have been eligible. Submitting false-information evidence is a covered affirmative act.
obligations.threshold: Willful (knowing) misrepresentation of a MATERIAL (outcome-determinative) fact = inadmissibility; any untrue statement of facts = revocation ground.
obligations.deadline: n/a (applies whenever the benefit is sought).
obligations.data_needed: petition_facts_verified_flag; supporting_doc_authenticity_flags; discrepancy_log (claimed vs actual: dates, duties, org structure, premises, payroll); site_visit_findings; prior_petition_disclosure_flag.
evidence_required: discrepancy_log (claimed vs actual: dates, duties, org structure, premises, payr

obligations.check: Individual (non-new-office) L-1 petition validity ≤3 years and matches the period of established need.
obligations.requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(7)(i)(A)(2): "An individual petition … shall be valid for the period of established need …, not to exceed three years, except where the beneficiary is coming to … open or to be employed in a new office." (New-office initial ≤1 year per (l)(7)(i)(A)(3).)
obligations.threshold: ≤3 years per increment (established); ≤1 year for new office. Extensions ((l)(15)(ii)) ≤2-year increments, within the 5/7-year ceilings.
obligations.deadline: Validity on the I-797; admission may not exceed validity.
obligations.data_needed: petition_type (individual|blanket); new_office_flag; established_need_period; approved_validity_start; approved_validity_end; extension_increment.

obligations.check: Recapture / commuter / intermittent exceptions to the 5- and 7-year caps are correctly applied.
obligations.requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(12)(ii): the max-stay limitations do NOT apply to aliens who do not reside continually in the U.S. and whose U.S. employment is "seasonal, intermittent, or consists of an aggregate of six months or less per year," nor to those who reside abroad and regularly commute to the U.S. for part-time employment. Must provide CLEAR AND CONVINCING proof (arrival/departure records, tax returns, foreign-employment records).
obligations.threshold: U.S. employment seasonal OR intermittent OR ≤6 months aggregate/year, no continual U.S. residence; OR resident-abroad regular commuter in part-time employment. Standard = clear and convincing.
obligations.deadline: n/a (status condition supporting continued eligibility past the nominal cap).
obligations.data_needed: exception_claimed_flag; us_employment_pattern (seasonal|intermittent|aggregate_days_per_year|commuter); us_residence_continual_flag; days_in_us_per_year; tax_returns; arrival_departure_records; foreign_residence_evidence.

obligations.check: An L-1 new-office extension is supported by evidence the office is actually doing business and (L-1A) now supports a managerial/executive position.
obligations.requirement: Per (l)(7)(i)(A)(3) + (l)(14)(ii): demonstrate it is doing business; evidence (A) entities still qualifying; (B) U.S. entity has been doing business for the previous year; (C) statement of the beneficiary's prior-year and extended duties; (D) staffing of the new operation (number of employees, position types, wages paid) where employed in a managerial/executive capacity; (E) financial status of the U.S. operation.
obligations.threshold: U.S. entity must have been "doing business" for the previous year; staffing/financials support the claimed capacity.
obligations.deadline: Filed before the 1-year new-office validity expires (extension only if the original validity has not expired, (l)(14)(i)).
obligations.data_needed: original_new_office_flag; current_doing_business_evidence (12 months); employee_count; positions_held; payroll_evidence; financial_statements; prior_year_duties; extended_duties; relationship_still_qualifying_flag; original_validity_expiry_date; extension_filing_date.

obligations.check: New-office L-1 petitions (U.S. entity doing business <1 year) meet the heightened evidentiary requirements and are approved for ≤1 year.
obligations.requirement: "New office" = doing business in the U.S. through a qualifying org for <1 year (8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(F)). For a manager/exec opening a new office ((l)(3)(v)): (A) sufficient physical premises secured; (B) the beneficiary had 1 continuous year (in the preceding 3) in an exec/managerial capacity AND the proposed employment involves exec/managerial authority over the new operation; and (C) within one year the U.S. operation will support an exec/managerial position. For SK new office ((l)(3)(vi)): (A) secured premises; (B) is/will be a qualifying organization; (C) financial ability to remunerate and commence doing business. Per (l)(7)(i)(A)(3), a new-office petition "may be approved for a period not to exceed one year."
obligations.threshold: U.S. doing-business < 1 year = new office. Initial validity ≤1 year (vs ≤3 for established offices).
obligations.deadline: Initial approval ≤1 year; within the first year the office must begin doing business to qualify for extension.
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(F); (l)(3)(v); (l)(3)(vi); (l)(7)(i)(A)(3); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 2.
obligations.data_needed: new_office_flag; us_entity_doing_business_start_date; physical_premises_secured_flag + lease_evidence; business_plan_flag (scope/org/financial_goals); us_investment_amount; foreign_entity_financial_ability_evidence; requested_validity_period; beneficiary_capacity.

obligations.check: Beneficiary has ≥1 continuous year of full-time employment abroad with a qualifying organization within the 3 years immediately preceding the petition (or admission).
obligations.requirement: An intracompany transferee is one who, "within three years preceding the time of his or her application for admission … has been employed abroad continuously for one year" by a qualifying organization. Individual-petition evidence must show ≥1 continuous year of full-time employment abroad within the 3 years preceding filing, in a managerial/executive/specialized-knowledge position.
obligations.threshold: 1 continuous year (12 months) of FULL-TIME employment, accrued WITHIN the 3-year window immediately preceding filing/admission. Reference = petition filing date (USCIS PM).
obligations.deadline: 3-year lookback measured backward from filing/admission. Time in the U.S. for the same employer and brief U.S. business/pleasure trips do NOT interrupt the year but are NOT counted toward it (they toll/extend the lookback).
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(A) (intracompany transferee / continuous year / tolling); (l)(3)(iii); (l)(3)(iv); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 2.
obligations.data_needed: foreign_employment_start_date; end_date; employment_full_time_flag; petition_filing_date; beneficiary_us_presence_periods (same employer); us_business_pleasure_trip_days; foreign_role_capacity (managerial|executive|specialized_knowledge).

obligations.check: A qualifying corporate relationship (parent/branch/subsidiary/affiliate) exists between the U.S. petitioner and the foreign entity.
obligations.requirement: Petitioner and the employing organization must be a "qualifying organization" meeting EXACTLY ONE of parent/branch/subsidiary/affiliate. Parent = "a firm, corporation, or other legal entity which has subsidiaries"; Branch = "an operating division or office of the same organization housed in a different location"; Subsidiary = parent owns, directly or indirectly, (a) >half + controls, (b) half + controls, (c) 50% of a 50-50 JV with equal control/veto, or (d) <half but in fact controls; Affiliate = two subsidiaries of the same parent/individual, two entities owned/controlled by the same group in approximately the same share, or the accounting-firm international-name arrangement.
obligations.threshold: Subsidiary: >50%+control; or 50%+control; or 50% of a 50-50 JV with equal control/veto; or <50% with de facto control. Affiliate: common ownership/control by the same parent/individual/proportionate group. Exactly ONE qualifying relationship.
obligations.deadline: n/a (structural; must exist at filing and be maintained).
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(G) (qualifying organization); (I) Parent; (J) Branch; (K) Subsidiary; (L) Affiliate; INA 101(a)(15)(L) (8 USC 1101(a)(15)(L)).
obligations.data_needed: petitioner_entity_id; foreign_entity_id; relationship_type; ownership_percent; control_evidence_flag (stock ledger / operating agreement / board minutes / audited financials / tax returns); joint_venture_flag; veto_power_flag; common_parent_or_individual_owner_id.
evidence_required: control_evidence_flag (stock ledger / operating agreement / board minutes / audi

obligations.check: The qualifying relationship is MAINTAINED, and the petitioner continues doing business in the U.S. AND at least one other country, throughout the entire L stay.
obligations.requirement: The qualifying organization must be "doing business as an employer in the United States and in at least one other country directly or through a parent, branch, affiliate, or subsidiary for the duration of the alien's stay." DOS: "The qualifying relationship must be maintained, and the employer must be doing business in both countries throughout the period of the L visa status." Ceasing to be a qualifying organization → revocation on notice.
obligations.threshold: "Doing business" = regular, systematic, and continuous provision of goods/services (NOT mere presence of an agent/office) in ≥2 countries, continuously.
obligations.deadline: Continuous — for the entire duration of stay.
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(G)(2) (doing business in 2 countries for duration); (l)(1)(ii)(H) (doing business definition); (l)(9)(iii)(A)(1) (revocation); DOS 9 FAM 402.12.
obligations.data_needed: us_doing_business_flag; foreign_doing_business_flag; foreign_entity_active_status; relationship_still_valid_flag; last_verified_date; corporate_change_events (merger|acquisition|dissolution|sale) with dates; revenue_or_activity_evidence_per_entity.

obligations.check: No automatic- or notice-revocation ground under 8 CFR 214.2(l)(9) is present; petitioner met its notify-of-changes duty.
obligations.requirement: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(9): immediately notify USCIS of changes affecting eligibility. (ii) Automatic revocation on withdrawal or (blanket) failure to request indefinite validity. (iii) Revocation on notice if: (1) entities no longer qualifying; (2) alien no longer eligible under 101(a)(15)(L); (3) a qualifying organization violated requirements; (4) statement of facts not true and correct; (5) approval involved gross error; or (6) no qualifying org used the blanket for three consecutive years.
obligations.threshold: Any (l)(9)(iii) ground = revocable on notice; withdrawal / failure to request indefinite blanket validity = automatic; blanket unused 3 consecutive years = revocable.
obligations.deadline: Notification "immediate"; blanket 3-consecutive-years-non-use is the bright-line for that ground.
obligations.data_needed: entity_still_qualifying_flag; beneficiary_still_eligible_flag; petition_facts_true_flag; petition_withdrawn_flag; blanket_indefinite_validity_requested_flag; blanket_years_since_last_use; employment_terms_change_flag; change_notified_flag.

obligations.check: (L-1A) The U.S. position is in a bona fide EXECUTIVE capacity per all four elements.
obligations.requirement: Executive capacity (8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(C)) = an assignment in which the employee primarily: (1) directs the management of the org or a major component/function; (2) establishes goals and policies; (3) exercises wide latitude in discretionary decision-making; and (4) receives only general supervision/direction from higher-level executives, the board, or stockholders.
obligations.threshold: "Primarily" on all four prongs (direct management at a major-component level; set goals/policies; wide discretion; only general supervision from board/top execs).
obligations.deadline: n/a (tested at each adjudication).
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(C); INA 101(a)(44)(B) (8 USC 1101(a)(44)(B)); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 3.
obligations.data_needed: requested_classification (L-1A); job_title; job_duties_text; org_chart; reports_to (board|stockholders|higher_exec); major_component_or_function_directed; policy_setting_authority_flag; discretionary_authority_scope.

obligations.check: (L-1A) The U.S. position is in a bona fide MANAGERIAL capacity per all four elements.
obligations.requirement: Managerial capacity (8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(B)) = an assignment in which the employee primarily: (1) manages the org/department/subdivision/function/component; (2) supervises and controls the work of other supervisory/professional/managerial employees, OR manages an essential function; (3) has authority to hire/fire or recommend personnel actions if another employee is directly supervised, or functions at a senior level (function/personnel manager); and (4) exercises discretion over day-to-day operations. A first-line supervisor is NOT managerial merely by supervising unless the supervised employees are professional.
obligations.threshold: "Primarily" on all four prongs. First-line supervisor of non-professionals = NOT managerial. Function manager allowed only if managing an essential function at a senior level.
obligations.deadline: n/a (tested at each adjudication; re-tested at extension and for new-office second-year).
obligations.citation: 8 CFR 214.2(l)(1)(ii)(B); INA 101(a)(44)(A) (8 USC 1101(a)(44)(A)); USCIS PM Vol 2 Part L Ch 3.
obligations.data_needed: requested_classification (L-1A); job_title; job_duties_text; org_chart; direct_reports_count; direct_reports_are_professional_flag; hire_fire_authority_flag; essential_function_managed; seniority_level; percent_time_on_managerial_duties.

obligations.check: (L-1A) Total stay in managerial/executive capacity ≤7 years.
obligations.requirement: Statute (INA 214(c)(2)(D)(i)): total authorized admission "shall not exceed 7 years." Reg (8 CFR 214.2(l)(12)(i)): one who has spent 7 years in a managerial/executive capacity may not be readmitted under (L) unless resided and physically present outside the U.S. for the immediate prior year.
